subject: BrightBridge: LangChain runtime tracing + embed SDK onramp
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@brightbridge.dev>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightBridge pilot proposal: LangChain runtime tracing + embed SDK onramp

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the intro at the summit last month. BrightBridge has been building a LangChain-first SDK for multi-tenant ISVs that bundles tracing hooks, candidate-ranking telemetry, and an embeddings runtime optimized for low-cost batching. We think Redwood's serving runtime (esp. the KV cache + fallback routing) would be a great fit to power an official BrightBridge "Redwood connector" we can ship to customers.

High-level ask: pilot a small integration that:
- plumbs Redwood tracing headers into our LangChain adapters (so platform traces span from host app -> SDK -> Redwood inference)
- maps our candidate-scoring telemetry to Redwood's trace schema (for per-route SLOs and quality alerts)
- validates that Redwood sandbox accepts our embedding batching and API keys under a multi-tenant flow

We attached a draft mutual action plan and a short tracing schema brief to this note. Proposed timeline: kickoff next week (21–23 Apr), 2-week tech spike, then co-demo and joint blog/press in May.

Can you point me to the right folks to scope infra creds, SSO for test tenants, and any security questionnaire we should expect?

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Integrations 
BrightBridge Labs

Attachments: BB-Redwood-MAP-20260411.pdf, tracing-schema-brief.md

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Alex — great to meet you at the summit too, and appreciate the clear asks. This is squarely aligned with our ISV partner program. Quick notes on next steps from our side:

- Security/compliance: Stephanie (cc) will own the checklist. BrightBridge can expect a short questionnaire and an evidence request (SOC2/infra diagram + sample audit log) — we support secure sandbox creds for pilots.
- Infra creds: we can provision a dedicated sandbox tenant with RBAC-limited API keys and a short-lived service token for tracer ingestion. See attached sandbox creds template.
- Technical owners: Karthik (cc) will own the tracer schema mapping and runtime perf goals.

We like your proposed timeline. Let's schedule a 45-minute kick in the 21–23 Apr range. Vanessa, can you help with co-marketing alignment and a lightweight SOW for the MAP?

Marissa

Subject: Re: BrightBridge pilot proposal: LangChain runtime tracing + embed SDK onramp

Alex — looping in a few technical clarifications so the spike scopes properly: we want to avoid any ingestion of PII in trace metadata. Can you confirm which candidate fields you currently emit in your SDK trace spans (user_id, session_id, prompt snippets, candidate_score, model_variant)? If we need to transform or hash fields on the client side, we should include that in the spike.

A couple of perf/compat items we should validate during the spike:
- embedding batching: your SDK should be able to send variable-size batched requests; we want to measure median and p95 token latency with typical batch sizes (8, 32, 128).
- KV cache warmup: ensure the LangChain adapters preserve the same prompt prefixes so our prefix caching can hit.

If you can share a minimal code sample we can exercise in our sandbox, we'll pre-provision SLO targets and a simple acceptance test.

—Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

On Sat, Apr 11, 2026 at 11:03 AM marissa.cole@redwood.ai wrote:
> Alex — great to meet you at the summit too...

From: Alex Rivera <alex@brightbridge.dev>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Venkataram <priya@brightbridge.dev>, integrations@brightbridge.dev
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightBridge pilot proposal: LangChain runtime tracing + embed SDK onramp

Karthik / Marissa — thanks. Quick answers inline:

- Trace fields: our current SDK emits: anonymous_user_id (hashed), session_id (rotation-enabled), prompt_excerpt (trimmed to 256 chars), candidate_score (float), model_label (string), latency_ms (int). We will stop sending any raw PII; anonymous_user_id is a salted hash.
- Code sample: attaching a small LangChain adapter patch that wraps RDWriter -> RedwoodHTTP client and emits the tracing headers as X-Request-Trace / X-Parent-Span.
- Batch behavior: our embed runtime supports batch sizes up to 128 and will fall back to streaming mode for larger jobs. We include a simple benchmark harness (see attached).

We are happy to sign an NDA/POA if needed for sandbox creds. Proposed kickoff: Wed, 22 Apr 10:00 PT — does that work for the Redwood team?

Best,
Alex

Attachments: ll_adapter_patch.diff, embed-bench-1k.csv

Alex — welcome aboard. A couple of items from GTM & SOW perspective:

1) Co-marketing: we typically do a joint one-pager + 1 blog post after the successful tech spike. If BrightBridge can provide a short customer quote (or a joint demo customer willing to be on the call), we can aim for publication late May.

2) SOW/credits: for pilot partners we grant $5k in hosted credits + 50% off dedicated burst capacity for the first month of an enterprise pilot (subject to funds approval). I'll draft a simple SOW that captures the MAP milestones and acceptance criteria (tracing spans validated, embedding latency targets met, docs + sample adapter merged).

3) Legal/Procurement: If you want an NDA/POA, we can circulate our standard partner NDA. For sandbox creds we need a signed POA or hubspot deal record.

I'll attach a one-page MAP template and a sample press checklist. Marissa — can you please attach the sandbox creds and assign Stephanie to the questionnaire?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner GTM
Redwood Inference
